Ranks of skeletal warriors stand in the gloom behind, rusted swords and shields raised, eye-sockets flickering with faint green fire.
A tide of shambling rotted zombies presses forward through the fog, countless and mindless, fading into the dark.
Drifting wraiths of pale luminous mist coil between the bone-towers, faces stretched in silent screams.
Bone-banners hang from jagged iron poles, stitched from grey skin, bearing sigils that shift and crawl like living things.
A wall of piled skulls stretches across the far ground, thousands deep, eye-sockets staring outward in every direction.
Skeletal steeds rear and stamp on cracked earth, their bare ribcages glowing faintly, draped in rotted barding and black leather.
Ghostly knights upon spectral horses drift above the ground, translucent and cold, armour flickering like candlelight in a storm.
Crawling severed hands scuttle across the bone-littered ground like pale spiders, fingers clacking against each other endlessly.
A swarm of flying bone-things circles high overhead, assembled from ribs and finger-joints, wings beating in eerie silence.
Tattered grave-shrouds billow on the cold wind between the ranks, trailing like smoke, as though the dead still wear them.
Impaled corpses line the processional way on tall stakes, arms dangling, heads bowed, each one reanimated and twitching faintly.
Floating spectral skulls drift at eye level throughout the host, jaws opening and closing, exhaling threads of cold green vapour.
A column of armoured skeleton knights marches in lockstep, their plate black with age, each carrying a long barbed lance.
Rotting siege-constructs of fused bone creak forward, massive and lurching, dragging chains attached to nothing, assembled by dark will alone.
Pale child-sized skeletons scurry between the legs of the larger dead, quick and unsettling, clutching small rusted daggers in bony fists.
A mass of tangled corpses has fused into one lurching mound, dozens of limbs reaching outward, driven by a single hunger.
Shadow-wolves built from darkness and scraps of bone prowl the flanks of the host, low to the ground, silent.
Skeletal archers stand in elevated rows on bone-scaffolding, arrows nocked in fleshless fingers, hollow sockets trained on the living ahead.
Enormous skeletal giants lumber between the ranks, assembled from the bones of many bodies, heads brushing the low poisoned clouds above.
Robed skeleton mages drift forward in a loose cluster, staffs topped with pulsing green orbs, dead fingers tracing patterns in the air.
A river of severed heads rolls and bounces across the ground, propelled by no wind, jaws snapping at anything within reach.
Chains of bound wailing ghosts trail behind an armoured lich-herald, the spirits stretched thin and screaming, tethered to his gauntleted wrist.
Masses of grave-dirt and bone splinters swirl in slow cyclones between formations, animated by ambient death-magic into grinding abrasive columns.
Skeletal war-drummers beat hollow ribcage-drums with femur sticks, keeping a thunderous rhythm that resonates deep in living chests like dread.
Translucent ghost-infantry march in perfect formation just above the ground, wearing the phantom-echoes of a dozen different fallen armies simultaneously.
